title: Object-Oriented Programming
tagline: Think in objects, not just functions
description: Classes and objects, the four pillars (encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism), composition over inheritance, interfaces vs abstract classes, object relationships, and common mistakes and interview questions, explained with real-life analogies and short TypeScript examples.

title: Clean Code & SOLID
description: Clean code, naming, functions, errors, KISS / DRY / YAGNI, refactoring, code profiling, Clean Architecture, and all five SOLID principles with practical examples.

title: Design Patterns
description: The 22 classic Gang of Four patterns in three families (creational, structural, behavioral), explained with real-life analogies and short JavaScript examples.

title: Software Architecture
description: Layered, MVC/MVVM, Clean Architecture, Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters), Onion, Domain-Driven Design, event-driven, microkernel, serverless, vertical slices and the modular monolith, plus how to choose between them.

title: Data Structures & Algorithms
description: Big-O, arrays, hash maps, linked lists, stacks, trees, heaps, graphs, sorting, binary search, recursion and dynamic programming, with a pattern cheat sheet for interviews.

title: Backend Engineering
description: How requests travel, API design (REST, GraphQL, gRPC), SQL vs NoSQL, concurrency, transactions, caching with Redis, queues, Kafka for event-driven services (outbox, idempotent consumers, retries and dead-letter topics), webhooks, resilience, authentication, scaling, Docker and backend languages.

title: Frontend Engineering
description: How browsers render, the JavaScript event loop, advanced TypeScript, React internals and hooks, scalable frontend architecture, state management, design systems and component libraries, Next.js and edge delivery, performance, security and testing.

title: Microservices
description: Monolith vs microservices, service boundaries, sync vs async communication, API gateways, resilience patterns, sagas, the outbox pattern, CQRS and observability.

title: Apache Kafka
description: Topics, partitions and offsets, producers, consumer groups, replication, delivery guarantees, and when to choose Kafka over RabbitMQ.

title: Linux & DevOps Deployment
tagline: From your laptop to a live server, safely
description: The Linux command line, users and permissions, processes and systemd, SSH and firewalls, Bash scripting and cron, Nginx with HTTPS, deploying a Node.js app to a VPS, CI/CD with GitHub Actions, Docker in production, zero-downtime releases and rollbacks, monitoring, logs and backups, and a troubleshooting playbook with interview questions. Then CI/CD fundamentals and pipeline design, Jenkins from install to production pipelines, and running Kafka in production from the operations side.

title: Kubernetes
description: From first Pod to production: cluster architecture, Deployments, Services and Ingress, storage, probes and Helm, then StatefulSets, Jobs, scheduling, networking and NetworkPolicies, troubleshooting, RBAC and security, CRDs and operators, GitOps, observability, upgrades and interview questions.

title: AWS for Developers
tagline: Build, deploy and secure cloud applications
description: A complete AWS path for developers: global infrastructure, IAM and least privilege, VPC networking, EC2 and Auto Scaling, load balancers and Route 53, S3, CloudFront, ECS on Fargate, RDS, Aurora and DynamoDB, Lambda and API Gateway, SQS/SNS/EventBridge, Cognito, Secrets Manager and KMS, CloudWatch observability, CI/CD with IaC, data pipelines and interview questions, then deeper topics: IAM policy evaluation and cross-account access, VPC endpoints and Transit Gateway, DynamoDB modeling and RDS scaling, event-driven patterns and Step Functions, multi-account governance and security operations, disaster recovery, ECS and EKS at scale, and cost optimization with the Well-Architected Framework.

title: Terraform
tagline: Infrastructure as code, from first plan to production
description: Learn Terraform from beginner to advanced with hands-on examples: a local first project, HCL, variables, providers, AWS resources, dependencies, loops, modules, remote state and locking, environment isolation, imports and refactoring, testing, secrets, CI/CD, troubleshooting, and a production capstone.

title: AI & Machine Learning
tagline: Understand models and build useful AI systems
description: A practical path through AI foundations, machine learning, data preparation, neural networks, transformers and LLMs, prompt design, embeddings and RAG, tool-using agents, evaluation, safety, and production operations. Start with the roadmap, then follow the lessons in order or jump to the skills your project needs.

title: Programming Languages
tagline: Write code with the right tools and mental models
description: JavaScript fundamentals and async code, TypeScript in practice, Node.js with Express and NestJS, Python with FastAPI and Django, Go with goroutines and Gin, and Rust ownership, traits and concurrency, plus how to choose a language.

title: System Design L6
tagline: Understand the scenario. Design the system. Prove it works.
description: Learn system design through realistic production scenarios. Trace requests, compare tradeoffs, recover from failures and validate every design.

title: Database Design & Performance
tagline: Model data, protect correctness, scale reads and writes
description: Relational modeling, normalization, ACID, indexes, query performance, replication, sharding, storage engines, and detailed DBMS interview preparation.

title: Job Preparation
tagline: From job plan to signed offer
description: A step-by-step path to your next developer job: plan your target role, build a resume that passes ATS, turn LinkedIn into an interview-call machine, find jobs on the best sites, use referrals and cold outreach, pick certifications that matter, prepare for coding, system design and behavioral rounds, ask smart questions, negotiate your offer, and start strong in your first 90 days.
